title: A Christmas Carol: Application Adventure
welcome_lead: Apply your knowledge to the three spirits, the Cratchits, and Scrooge's transformation.
meta_desc: Application practice on Dickens's three ghosts, Tiny Tim, Fred, and Scrooge's moral journey.
final_note: You can now tie ghost to lesson. Stretch yourself with context next.

concepts.def: A child-like spirit showing Scrooge his school and Belle.
A jolly giant revealing the Cratchits and Fred's party.
A silent black-robed phantom showing Scrooge's grave.
Bob's sickly son; symbol of vulnerable poverty.
Scrooge's nephew; embodies kindness Scrooge rejects.
Two children hidden under the Present Ghost's robe.

walkthroughs.body_html: The first spirit takes Scrooge to his lonely boarding school, to Fezziwig's joyful ball, and to Belle leaving him for loving gold more than her. Memory becomes the first crack in Scrooge's hardened heart. He weeps for the child he was and the love he traded for profit.

The Present Ghost shows the Cratchits' modest feast and Fred's warm party. Tiny Tim's frailty makes Scrooge ask if he will live. The ghost throws Scrooge's own words back at him: 'decrease the surplus population'. Beneath the robe Dickens reveals Ignorance and Want, the moral cost of neglect.

The silent phantom shows a man whose death brings only relief. Scrooge sees his own unmourned grave and Tim's empty chair. Terror finally breaks him. He vows to honour Christmas 'in my heart' and keep all three lessons, completing the redemption arc.
